results.label: Definition 1.1 (Learning model).
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem1] Definition 1.1 (Learning model).
 [S1.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
A learner receives  $n$  independent copies of an unknown  $\rho\in\mathcal{D}_{d,r}$  and returns an arbitrary density matrix  $\widehat{\sigma}\in\mathcal{D}_{d}$ . Its output need not have rank at most  $r$ . For a loss  $L$ , the constant-confidence requirement is
 [S1.E6] 
 $\inf_{\rho\in\mathcal{D}_{d,r}}\mathbb{P}_{\rho}\{L(\rho,\widehat{\sigma})\leq\varepsilon\}\geq\frac{2}{3}.$ (6)

Collective measurements permit any positive operator-valued measure (POVM) on  $\rho^{\otimes n}$ . Adaptive one-copy measurements permit a POVM on each next copy chosen from previous classical outcomes and internal randomness, but no quantum memory coupling different copies. All consumed copies, including rejected projection outcomes, count toward  $n$ . Measurements and estimators are measurable.

results.label: Theorem 1.2 (Main lower bounds).
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem2] Theorem 1.2 (Main lower bounds).
 [S1.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
There are universal constants  $c,\varepsilon_{0}>0$  such that, for all integers  $d\geq 2$ ,  $1\leq r\leq d$ , and  $0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_{0}$ ,
 [S1.EGx3] 
 $\displaystyle N_{\rm coll}(\mathcal{D}_{d,r},\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{B}},\varepsilon)$  $\displaystyle\geq c\frac{\sqrt{r}\,d^{3/2}}{\varepsilon},$  $\displaystyle N_{\rm one}(\mathcal{D}_{d,r},\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{B}},\varepsilon)$  $\displaystyle\geq c\frac{r^{3/2}d^{3/2}}{\varepsilon},$ (7)

 $\displaystyle N_{\rm coll}(\mathcal{D}_{d,r},\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}},\varepsilon)$  $\displaystyle\geq c\frac{d^{2}}{\varepsilon^{2}},$  $\displaystyle N_{\rm one}(\mathcal{D}_{d,r},\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}},\varepsilon)$  $\displaystyle\geq c\frac{rd^{2}}{\varepsilon^{2}}.$ (8)

For  $1\leq r\leq d/2$ , the same bounds hold on the smaller family  $\rho=P/r$ , where  $P$  ranges over rank- $r$  orthogonal projectors.

results.label: Theorem 1.3 (Upper bounds).
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem3] Theorem 1.3 (Upper bounds).
 [S1.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
For  $0<\varepsilon\leq 1$  and  $0<\delta<1/2$ , let  $L_{0}=\lceil\log_{2}(16d/\varepsilon)\rceil$ . There are learners that succeed with probability at least  $1-\delta$  uniformly on  $\mathcal{D}_{d,r}$ , with the following copy bounds:
 [S1.EGx4] 
Bures, collective: $\displaystyle O\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{r}\,d^{3/2}}{\varepsilon}L_{0}^{2}\log\frac{L_{0}}{\delta}\right),$ (9)

Bures, adaptive one-copy: $\displaystyle O\!\left(\frac{r^{3/2}d^{3/2}}{\varepsilon}L_{0}^{2}\log\frac{2dL_{0}}{\delta}\right),$ (10)

Right-inverse, collective: $\displaystyle O\!\left(\frac{d^{2}}{\varepsilon^{2}}\log\frac{1}{\delta}\right),$ (11)

Right-inverse, adaptive one-copy: $\displaystyle O\!\left(\frac{rd^{2}}{\varepsilon^{2}}\log\frac{2d}{\delta}\right).$ (12)

For pure inputs, collective measurements achieve  $O(d^{3/2}/\varepsilon)$  for  $\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{B}}$  and  $O(d^{2}/\varepsilon^{2})$  for  $\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}}$  at constant confidence, without logarithmic factors.

results.label: Lemma 1.4 (Two comparison inequalities).
results.statement:
[S1.Thmtheorem4] Lemma 1.4 (Two comparison inequalities).
 [S1.Thmtheorem4.p1] 
For density matrices,
 [S1.E13] 
 $\mathsf{b}(\rho,\sigma)^{2}\leq\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{B}}(\rho\,\|\,\sigma),\qquad\left\lVert\rho-\sigma\right\rVert_{1}^{2}\leq\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{B}}(\rho\,\|\,\sigma).$ (13)

Moreover  $\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{B}}$  is the largest classical chi-squared divergence obtainable by measuring the pair of states with the same POVM.

results.label: Lemma 2.1 (Grassmann coordinates and a matrix ball).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 2.1 (Grassmann coordinates and a matrix ball).
 [S2.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Let
 [S2.Ex8] 
 $V_{s,r}=\operatorname{vol}\{Z\in\mathbb{C}^{s\times r}:Z^{*}Z<\mathrm{I}_{r}\}.$ 

Then
 [S2.E14] 
 $V_{s,r}=\pi^{q}\prod_{j=1}^{r}\frac{(j-1)!}{(s+j-1)!},\qquad\left(\frac{\pi}{2s}\right)^{q}\leq V_{s,r}\leq\left(\frac{\pi e}{s}\right)^{q}.$ (14)

In the graph chart
 [S2.E15] 
 $U_{X}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathrm{I}_{r}\\ X\end{pmatrix}(\mathrm{I}_{r}+X^{*}X)^{-1/2},\qquad P_{X}=U_{X}U_{X}^{*},$ (15)

Haar measure has density
 [S2.E16] 
 $\frac{d\mu}{dX}=V_{s,r}^{-1}\det(\mathrm{I}_{r}+X^{*}X)^{-d}.$ (16)

If  $U$  is a Haar orthonormal  $r$ -frame in  $\mathbb{C}^{r+s}$  and  $Z$  denotes its last  $s$  rows, then  $Z$  is uniform on the matrix ball in Equation 14.

results.label: Lemma 2.2 (Tail mass and subspace distance).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 2.2 (Tail mass and subspace distance).
 [S2.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
If  $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/4$  and  $\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{B}}(P/r\,\|\,\sigma)\leq\varepsilon$ , then
 [S2.E17] 
 $a\leq\varepsilon,\qquad t:=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(P(\mathrm{I}-Q))}{r}\leq 4\varepsilon.$ (17)

The same holds under a  $\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}}\leq\varepsilon$  guarantee.

results.label: Lemma 2.3 (Uniform tail eigenvalues maximize a volume).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem3] Lemma 2.3 (Uniform tail eigenvalues maximize a volume).
 [S2.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
For fixed  $K>0$  and  $\operatorname{Tr}A=a$ , the Lebesgue volume of  $\{Z\in\mathbb{C}^{s\times r}:H_{A}(Z)\leq K\}$  is at most its value at  $A=(a/s)\mathrm{I}_{s}$ .

results.label: Theorem 2.4 (Haar volumes of loss balls).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem4] Theorem 2.4 (Haar volumes of loss balls).
 [S2.Thmtheorem4.p1] 
For  $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/4$  and any density matrix  $\sigma$ ,
 [S2.EGx5] 
 $\displaystyle\mu\{P:\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{B}}(P/r\,\|\,\sigma)\leq\varepsilon\}$  $\displaystyle\leq\left(6e\,\varepsilon\sqrt{r/s}\right)^{q},$ (19)

 $\displaystyle\mu\{P:\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}}(P/r\,\|\,\sigma)\leq\varepsilon\}$  $\displaystyle\leq\left(18e\,r\varepsilon^{2}/s\right)^{q}.$ (20)

results.label: Corollary 2.5 (Euclidean volumes in a fixed local chart).
results.statement:
[S2.Thmtheorem5] Corollary 2.5 (Euclidean volumes in a fixed local chart).
 [S2.Thmtheorem5.p1] 
Let  $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/4$  and restrict  $X$  in Equation 15 to  $\left\lVert X\right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq 1/2$ . For every fixed estimate  $\sigma$ , let  $v_{\rm B}$  and  $v_{\rm R}$  be the Lebesgue volumes of the two successful parameter sets in this chart. Then
 [S2.E22] 
 $v_{\rm B}^{1/q}\leq C\frac{\varepsilon\sqrt{r/s}}{s},\qquad v_{\rm R}^{1/q}\leq C\frac{r\varepsilon^{2}}{s^{2}}.$ (22)

results.label: Lemma 3.1 (Fisher information and volume).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 3.1 (Fisher information and volume).
 [S3.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Let  $p\geq 3$ , let  $\sqrt{f}\in H^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{p})$  vanish outside a compact set, and let  $S$  have Lebesgue volume  $v$ . Then
 [S3.E23] 
 $\int_{S}f\leq\frac{v^{2/p}}{p}\,\mathcal{I}(f).$ (23)

An absolute constant in place of  $1$  would give the same conclusions below.

results.label: Lemma 3.2 (Posterior information identity).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 3.2 (Posterior information identity).
 [S3.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
Under the preceding conditions, assume  $\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\operatorname{Tr}F_{\theta}<\infty$ . Then
 [S3.E24] 
 $\mathbb{E}_{Y}\mathcal{I}(\pi(\cdot\mid Y))=\mathcal{I}(\pi)+\mathbb{E}_{\theta\sim\pi}\operatorname{Tr}F_{\theta}.$ (24)

In particular, almost every posterior has a compactly supported  $H^{1}$  square root whenever the right-hand side is finite.

results.label: Corollary 3.3 (Bayesian success bound).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem3] Corollary 3.3 (Bayesian success bound).
 [S3.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
Under the preceding conditions, let  $p\geq 3$ . Suppose that every estimate’s successful parameter set within the prior support has Lebesgue volume at most  $v$ . Then
 [S3.E25] 
 $\mathbb{P}\{\text{success}\}\leq\frac{v^{2/p}}{p}\left(\mathcal{I}(\pi)+\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\operatorname{Tr}F_{\theta}\right).$ (25)

results.label: Lemma 3.4 (Local prior).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem4] Lemma 3.4 (Local prior).
 [S3.Thmtheorem4.p1] 
On  $\mathbb{C}^{s\times r}\cong\mathbb{R}^{2rs}$ ,  $r\leq s$ , there is a prior supported on  $\left\lVert X\right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq 1/2$  such that
 [S3.E26] 
 $\mathcal{I}(\pi)\leq C_{0}rs^{2}.$ (26)

Its square root is compactly supported and belongs to  $H^{1}$ .

results.label: Lemma 3.5 (Collective and adaptive information budgets).
results.statement:
[S3.Thmtheorem5] Lemma 3.5 (Collective and adaptive information budgets).
 [S3.Thmtheorem5.p1] 
For the  $p=2rs$  real coordinates of  $X$ :
 [S3.EGx7] 
 $\displaystyle\operatorname{Tr}F_{X}$  $\displaystyle\leq\frac{4np}{r}=8ns$  $\displaystyle\text{for any collective measurement on $n$ copies},$ (28)

 $\displaystyle\operatorname{Tr}F_{X}$  $\displaystyle\leq\frac{4ns}{r}$  $\displaystyle\text{for any adaptive one-copy protocol}.$ (29)

results.label: Lemma 5.1 (Shell accounting).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem1] Lemma 5.1 (Shell accounting).
 [S5.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For each stage  $j$ , assign to it all matrix entries with one index in the newly frozen shell and both indices in the active subspace at that stage. The sum of  $|\rho_{uv}-A_{uv}|^{2}$  over these ordered entries is at most  $\eta_{j}$ . Their contribution to
 [S5.Ex45] 
 $E_{\rm B}(\rho,A):=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl[(\rho-A)\mathcal{J}_{A}^{-1}(\rho-A)\bigr]$ 

is therefore at most  $2\eta_{j}/\lambda_{j}$ . Every entry outside the final active block is assigned exactly once.

results.label: Lemma 5.2 (Exact normalization formula).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem2] Lemma 5.2 (Exact normalization formula).
 [S5.Thmtheorem2.p1] 
Let  $\rho$  have trace one, let  $A>0$ , and set  $t=\operatorname{Tr}A$ . For either  $E_{\rm B}(\rho,A)$  as above or  $E_{\rm R}(\rho,A)=\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho-A)^{2}A^{-1}]$ ,
 [S5.E40] 
 $\chi^{2}(\rho\,\|\,A/t)=tE(\rho,A)-(t-1)^{2},\qquad(t-1)^{2}\leq tE(\rho,A).$ (40)

In particular,  $E\leq 1/2$  implies  $t\leq 2$  and  $\chi^{2}(\rho\,\|\,A/t)\leq 2E$ .

results.label: Lemma 5.3 (One-copy submatrix routine).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem3] Lemma 5.3 (One-copy submatrix routine).
 [S5.Thmtheorem3.p1] 
Let  $0<\beta<1/2$  and  $\eta>0$ . If  $W^{2}\leq\eta$ , the zero estimate suffices. Otherwise the construction above outputs a positive semidefinite estimate with squared Frobenius error at most  $\eta$ , with probability at least  $1-\beta$ , using
 [S5.E44] 
 $O\!\left[\left(\frac{rkW}{\eta}+k\sqrt{\frac{r}{\eta}}\right)\log\frac{2k}{\beta}\right]$ (44)

copies. The rank bound can be replaced by  $\min\{r,k\}$ . In the nontrivial case  $W^{2}>\eta$ , the displayed bound is at least a positive constant, so rounding the copy count to an integer does not change its order.

results.label: Lemma 5.4 (Frobenius error to right-inverse chi-squared).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem4] Lemma 5.4 (Frobenius error to right-inverse chi-squared).
 [S5.Thmtheorem4.p1] 
Let  $\widehat{\rho}$  be a density matrix and  $\sigma=(1-\alpha)\widehat{\rho}+\alpha\mathrm{I}_{d}/d$ ,  $0<\alpha<1$ . Then
 [S5.E47] 
 $\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}}(\rho\,\|\,\sigma)\leq\frac{2d}{\alpha}\left\lVert\rho-\widehat{\rho}\right\rVert_{\mathrm{F}}^{2}+\frac{2\alpha}{1-\alpha}.$ (47)

In particular,  $\alpha=\varepsilon/8$  and  $\left\lVert\rho-\widehat{\rho}\right\rVert_{\mathrm{F}}^{2}\leq\varepsilon^{2}/(64d)$  imply  $\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}}\leq\varepsilon$  for  $0<\varepsilon\leq 1$ .

results.label: Proposition 5.5 (Collective submatrix routine).
results.statement:
[S5.Thmtheorem5] Proposition 5.5 (Collective submatrix routine).
 [S5.Thmtheorem5.p1] 
Let  $R$  be a positive semidefinite block of dimension  $k$  and mass  $w\leq W\leq 1$ . For  $\eta>0$  and  $0<\beta<1/2$ , a collective routine returns a positive semidefinite estimate with squared Frobenius error at most  $\eta$ , with probability at least  $1-\beta$ , using
 [S5.E49] 
 $O\!\left(\frac{kW}{\eta}\log\frac{1}{\beta}\right)$ (49)

full copies. If  $W^{2}\leq\eta$ , no copies are required.

results.label: Theorem A.1 (Minimax expected right-inverse loss for pure states).
results.statement:
[A1.Thmtheorem1] Theorem A.1 (Minimax expected right-inverse loss for pure states).
 [A1.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
For  $n\geq 0$  copies of an unknown pure state in dimension  $d$  and arbitrary collective measurements,
 [A1.E50] 
 $\inf_{\text{learners}}\sup_{\psi}\mathbb{E}_{\psi}\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}}(|\psi\rangle\!\langle\psi|\,\|\,\widehat{\sigma})=\frac{(\sqrt{n+1}+d-1)^{2}}{n+d}-1.$ (50)

results.label: Proposition B.1 (Common center of two flat states).
results.statement:
[A2.Thmtheorem1] Proposition B.1 (Common center of two flat states).
 [A2.Thmtheorem1.p1] 
Let  $P,Q$  be rank- $r$  projectors with principal angles  $\theta_{1},\ldots,\theta_{r}$ , in dimension at least  $2r$ . Then
 [A2.EGx10] 
 $\displaystyle\inf_{\sigma}\max\{\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}}(P/r\,\|\,\sigma),\chi^{2}_{\mathrm{R}}(Q/r\,\|\,\sigma)\}$ 

 $\displaystyle\qquad=\left(\frac{1}{r}\sum_{i=1}^{r}\sqrt{1+\sin\theta_{i}}\right)^{2}-1\ \geq\ (\sqrt{2}-1)\frac{\left\lVert P-Q\right\rVert_{1}}{r}.$ (52)

The same minimum is obtained if the maximum is replaced by the arithmetic mean. A minimizing state is proportional to  $\sqrt{P+Q}$  on its support.
